recognize_zh: CD5 免疫染色中，真皮內小到中型淋巴球絕大多數呈強且清楚的細胞膜陽性，只剩少數藍色陰性細胞群（多為 B 細胞區）；CD5 保留表現是 CD4+ 小/中型 T 細胞增生性疾病常見的表型，與常有泛 T 標記缺失的侵襲性 T 細胞淋巴瘤不同。
features: Dense infiltrate of small to medium-sized lymphoid cells
Strong, crisp membranous CD5 staining in the majority of cells
Intervening pockets of CD5-negative cells, likely B cells and histiocytes
Positive cells show slight variation in size, including some medium-sized cells
No evidence of loss of CD5 in the dominant population
describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain for CD5 on a skin biopsy shows a dense lymphoid infiltrate in which the majority of small to medium-sized cells show strong membranous staining, with interspersed pockets of CD5-negative cells. There is no apparent loss of CD5 in the dominant T-cell population. Retention of CD5 and other pan-T antigens with only variable CD7 loss is typical of primary cutaneous CD4-positive small/medium T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder. Findings are consistent with a CD5-positive T-cell-rich infiltrate in this context.

ddx.dx: Primary cutaneous peripheral T-cell lymphoma, NOS
ddx.vs: Aggressive cutaneous PTCL typically has larger, more pleomorphic cells exceeding 30%, ulceration and frequent loss of multiple pan-T antigens, rather than retained CD5.
CLL cells are CD5-positive B cells that coexpress CD20, CD23 and LEF1, whereas this CD5-positive population is CD3-positive T cells.
Mycosis fungoides can retain CD5 but is defined by epidermotropic CD4+ T cells in a patch/plaque clinical setting.
